translation_en:
…knew only to fulfill their loyal duty of guarding the throne; what more could they have sought? Moreover, when the former kings regulated the people’s obligations, they required them to pay taxes to support the government. Yet the apportioned requisitions and miscellaneous levies introduced in recent times are ten times those of old. Who has earnestly sought reductions on their behalf to relieve their distress? Not only has no one done so, but officials exploit these demands as a pretext for personal gain. How, then, could the people fail to leave their homes and wander?

When the former kings regulated military obligations, they required soldiers to bear shields and spears to defend the altars of soil and grain. Yet in recent years public construction and private labor services have arisen one after another throughout the various regions. Who has shown solicitude for the soldiers and spared their strength? Not only has no one done so, but officials seize these opportunities to enrich themselves. How, then, could the soldiers fail to desert?

Although the people of Jiangnan may appear somewhat prosperous, the demands for which they must find funds are onerous. They have nevertheless had the good fortune of repeated abundant harvests in their fields, yet their annual income barely meets a single year’s expenses. Should floods or droughts unexpectedly occur, how could they sustain themselves? If this is the condition of the region on whose supplies the state depends, how much worse must it be in other prefectures?

Although the troops of the Three Frontiers may appear to have long been well ordered, they are exhausted by the services demanded of them. They have nevertheless happened upon a period of decline among the foreign peoples, yet the soldiers stationed along the frontier are barely sufficient to meet an emergency in a single area. Should those peoples harbor treacherous intentions, how could the troops defend against them? If this is the condition of strategically vital places, how much worse must it be in the other garrisons?

This cannot but trouble Your Majesty, who rises before dawn and eats only late in the day in concern for affairs of state. For the present, no course is better than putting our own governance in order at…

title: 弘治十二年會試錄
text:
朝廷之上以清其本源之地遠述三王上法
皇祖
聖天子宰制于上諸大臣奉行于下撙節
國用而無事乎虛文慎重工作而無牽于浮
議明示有司務養民以為心而同其好惡
定主戸客戶之制使勞者定散者還課其
政為殿最而凡貪墨者必黜勞于撫字者
有褒則富庶之效可期何水旱之足憂乎
嚴飭將臣務愛兵以為事而同其甘苦節
===
屯兵練兵之勞使亡者歸闕者完稽其實
為功罪而凡掊尅者必懲勤于撫練者有
賞則強盛之效可望何邊警之足慮乎夫
如是不獨江南之民益裕而天下之民可
裕也不獨三邊之兵益足而天下之兵可
足也何內之不實何外之不固而三代之
令猷
皇祖之盛治將復見于
今日矣管見如此而尤有進於是者不敢不終

punctuated: 朝廷之上，以清其本源之地，遠述三王，上法皇祖。聖天子宰制于上，諸大臣奉行于下，撙節國用而無事乎虛文，慎重工作而無牽于浮議。明示有司，務養民以為心，而同其好惡；定主戸客戶之制，使勞者定，散者還；課其政為殿最，而凡貪墨者必黜，勞于撫字者有褒，則富庶之效可期，何水旱之足憂乎？嚴飭將臣，務愛兵以為事，而同其甘苦；節屯兵練兵之勞，使亡者歸，闕者完；稽其實為功罪，而凡掊尅者必懲，勤于撫練者有賞，則強盛之效可望，何邊警之足慮乎？夫如是，不獨江南之民益裕，而天下之民可裕也；不獨三邊之兵益足，而天下之兵可足也。何內之不實，何外之不固？而三代之令猷、皇祖之盛治，將復見于今日矣。管見如此，而尤有進於是者，不敢不終
translation_en:
…at the imperial court, thereby purifying the source from which government flows, carrying forward the ways of the Three Kings of antiquity and taking the imperial ancestor as the supreme model. Let the sagely Son of Heaven direct affairs above and the great ministers carry them out below, economizing on state expenditure without busying themselves with empty formalities, and undertaking construction works cautiously without being swayed by shallow opinions. Clearly instruct the responsible officials to make nurturing the people their concern and to share their likes and dislikes. Establish regulations for registered local and sojourning households, so that those worn down by toil may settle securely and those dispersed may return. Assess officials’ administration and rank their performance from worst to best: invariably dismiss the corrupt and commend those who labor to care for the people. Then prosperity and a flourishing population may be expected. What cause would floods or droughts give for anxiety?

Strictly admonish the commanders to make caring for their soldiers their business and to share their comforts and hardships. Moderate the burdens of garrison service and military training, so that deserters return and vacancies are filled. Investigate actual performance to determine merit and fault: invariably punish those who exploit the soldiers and reward those diligent in caring for and training them. Then military strength and vigor may be expected. What cause would border alarms give for concern?

If this is done, not only will the people of Jiangnan become more prosperous, but the people throughout the realm can prosper; not only will the forces of the Three Frontiers become more amply supplied, but the forces throughout the realm can have enough. How could the interior fail to be substantial in its resources, or the frontiers fail to be secure? The excellent policies of the Three Dynasties and the magnificent government of the imperial ancestor will appear again in our own day. Such is my limited view; yet there is a further point beyond this, and I dare not leave unfinished…

Amid peace, prosperity, and harmony, there should also emerge great achievements that invigorate and renew, amply fulfilling the hopes of soldiers and common people. Is this not the moment for them? 朝純且備矣隆古盛時道行化
成非正學不以教而在所取
以見用者多吉人也周末治

translation_en: …in our dynasty have become pure and complete. In the flourishing age of high antiquity, the Way prevailed and moral transformation was accomplished. Nothing but orthodox learning was used in teaching, and those selected for service were mostly worthy men. At the end of the Zhou, good governance declined. Confucius and Mencius carried forward the tradition of the past, but government and teaching became separated, and scholars lost their proper role. More than a thousand years later, in the Song, the Cheng masters and Zhu Xi arose, and the Way was once again made clear. Yet what emerged from the instruction of these masters and their disciples for practical use in the world was rejected by the rulers of the time and prohibited. They called its teachings “distorted doctrines” and branded its adherents practitioners of “false learning.” These great worthies and gentlemen, however, were deeply concerned for the world and deplored the failings of the selection of scholars. They therefore set out practicable standards, procedures, and regulations, preserving them in a work entitled Private Proposals (Siyi). The Way had been made clear, yet they were unable to put even a little of it into practice in their own age. Could it be that…

高皇帝受命殪戎為中夏主

translation_en: …was Heaven’s transformation indeed awaiting its proper time? Our Emperor Gao received the mandate, destroyed the enemy forces, and became lord of the Central Lands. Uniquely endowed with supreme wisdom, he bore the weighty responsibilities of ruler and teacher. The successive sage emperors have guarded the Way with utmost care. Everything formerly called “distorted teachings” has now been established as the curriculum for scholars, without dissent. If anyone dares to disparage Cheng and Zhu, his writings are burned and he is excluded. For recruitment through the examinations, due consideration was given to the Private Deliberations (Siyi) in framing regulations, which were inscribed in the statutes to enjoin their perpetual observance. Thus scholars advance entirely through the proper path. The greatest among them assist His Majesty in presiding over affairs according to the Way; the rest are assessed and selected according to the extent of their learning. Never has the Way of the former kings been more fully elucidated and manifested in practice than today. It is fitting that scholars should not be deprived of their proper employment, and that government and moral instruction throughout the realm should be so pure and …

title: 弘治十二年會試錄
text:
備哉惟茲試上距洪武開科
三十有九矣自
陛下嗣大歴服則一紀矣士之被
道化而興者視前加盛蓋其
見錄者蔚乎炳然無詭道之
言故因以察其無倍道之行
干異時者加多乎可知已既
===
===
試之嗣月
陛下將親策之士以其所誦法者
而登對焉
賜之甲等以次入官其尚無負
所教與所取而用之者庶可
以保正學倫吉人希蹤往哲
而俾斯文之足徵也哉臣無

translation_en:
…complete indeed! This examination is the thirty-ninth since examinations were inaugurated in the Hongwu reign. A full cycle of twelve years has passed since Your Majesty succeeded to the great imperial charge. Scholars who have risen under the transforming influence of the Way are more numerous than before. Those selected are splendidly distinguished, and their words do not deviate from the Way. From this one may discern that their conduct does not contravene the Way either; that such men have become more numerous than in former times [?] may thus be known.
In the month following this examination, Your Majesty will personally examine them with policy questions. The scholars will come forward to answer on the basis of what they have studied and taken as their models. They will be awarded ranked grades and enter official service in due order. May they prove worthy of the instruction they have received and of those who selected and employed them! Thus may they preserve orthodox learning, take their place among worthy men, aspire to follow the wise men of the past, and furnish ample testimony to this cultural tradition. Your unworthy servant …

講筵二十年来仰窺

簡賢圖治比隆先王而升斯
世于大猷也輒僭有所述寘

告成而為天下誦焉
===

似，獲侍講筵二十年来，仰窺睿學惓惓于尊孔子、服程朱之說，簡賢圖治，比隆先王，而升斯世于大猷也。輒僭有所述，寘錄尾，以告成，而為天下誦焉。

通議大夫、掌詹事府事、禮部右侍郎兼翰林院學士程敏政謹序。
translation_en:
…unworthy as I am, I have had the privilege of attending Your Majesty’s lectures for twenty years. I have reverently observed Your Majesty’s sagely learning: your earnest devotion to honoring Confucius and following the teachings of Cheng and Zhu, selecting worthy men and seeking good government, matching the ancient kings in greatness, and raising this age to the great Way. I have therefore ventured to compose these remarks and place them at the end of this record, to announce its completion and proclaim this to all under Heaven.

Respectfully composed as a preface by Cheng Minzheng, Grand Master for Thorough Counsel, in charge of the Household Administration of the Heir Apparent, Right Vice Minister of Rites, and concurrently Academician of the Hanlin Academy.
